terra.problem: Saying Paul already knows the people adds a detail. He wants to visit the brothers in towns where they proclaimed the word.
The quoted words are the narrator's explanation, not something Paul says.
“Barnabas didn't give up on Mark” asserts Barnabas's attitude without the text saying it.
The cookie-sheet joke doesn't connect logically to choosing between islands.
Calling Silas a leader among the brothers is a fact from outside the passage and needs its own reference, such as Acts 15:22.
The oven comparison doesn't fit: an oven bakes dough, rather than strengthening it in the way Paul strengthened the churches.
The passage doesn't call Timothy young. If using that detail from elsewhere, it needs a reference.
The text says the Jews in the area all knew Timothy's father was Greek, not everyone in the area.
The explanation is flat and mostly repeats that the man was standing in the vision.
Calling Galilee Jesus' home region brings in a Bible fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The text doesn't say the team combined the vision and the earlier closed routes to reach its conclusion.
The passage says the team concluded God had called them after the vision; it doesn't directly state that the call came in the vision.
